Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1196
A randomized trial compares a new antihypertensive drug with placebo. Mean systolic blood pressure falls 9 mm Hg more in the drug group than in the placebo group. The investigators set alpha at 0.05 and report p = 0.03. Which of the following best interprets this p-value?
A. The drug lowers blood pressure in 97% of patients
B. The power of the study is 97%
C. The probability of a Type II error is 3%
D. There is a 3% probability of observing a difference this large or larger if the null hypothesis is true
E. Three percent of patients in the drug group had no response
Answer: D
Why this is correct: The p-value is the probability of observing a result as extreme or more extreme than the one found, assuming the null hypothesis (no real difference) is true. Because 0.03 is below the alpha of 0.05, the investigators reject the null hypothesis.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1197
A small trial concludes that a new sepsis drug significantly reduces 28-day mortality compared with placebo (p = 0.04), and the null hypothesis is rejected. Three much larger, well-designed trials later show that the drug has no effect on mortality. Assuming the later trials are correct, which of the following best describes the result of the original trial?
A. Bias
B. Correct decision
C. Low power
D. Type I error
E. Type II error
Answer: D
Why this is correct: A Type I error is rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true. The first trial concluded there was a difference when there truly wasn't one. The probability of this error is alpha.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1198
A pilot study of 40 patients finds no statistically significant difference in wound healing between a new dressing and standard gauze, and the investigators fail to reject the null hypothesis. A later trial of 4,000 patients shows the new dressing clearly speeds healing. Assuming the larger trial is correct, which of the following best describes the pilot study's conclusion?
A. Bias
B. Correct decision
C. Correlation without causation
D. Type I error
E. Type II error
Answer: E
Why this is correct: A Type II error is accepting (failing to reject) the null hypothesis when it is false. There really was a difference, and the pilot study missed it. Its probability is beta, and a study with low power is more likely to make this error.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1199
A research group is designing a randomized, placebo-controlled trial of a new vaccine against respiratory syncytial virus in 6,000 older adults. Before starting the trial, investigators decide that they are willing to accept a 5% probability of concluding the vaccine prevents infection when it actually does not. Which of the following terms describes this 5% value?
A. Alpha
B. Beta
C. P-value
D. Power
E. Specificity
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Concluding the vaccine works when it doesn't is rejecting a true null hypothesis, which is a Type I error. Alpha is the probability of a Type I error, and investigators set it before the study begins.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1200
A research team designs a trial of a new asthma inhaler. They calculate that, with their planned sample size, there is a 20% probability of failing to detect a true difference in exacerbation rates if one exists. Which of the following is the power of this study?
A. 0.05
B. 0.20
C. 0.80
D. 0.95
E. 1.20
Answer: C
Why this is correct: The 20% probability of missing a true difference is beta (the probability of a Type II error). Power is 1 − beta, so power = 1 − 0.20 = 0.80.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1201
Two trials are testing the same new migraine drug. The investigators of the first trial report that their study has high power, and the investigators of the second trial report that their study has low power. Compared with the second trial, the first trial has a higher probability of which of the following?
A. Detecting an effect if one exists
B. Detecting an effect when none exists
C. Failing to detect an effect that exists
D. Obtaining a p-value below 0.05 regardless of the true effect
E. Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Power (1 − beta) is the ability to detect an effect if one exists. Higher power means a lower chance of a Type II error.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1202
A drug regulatory committee is reviewing a new medication. Members discuss two possible mistakes: approving a drug that actually doesn't work, or rejecting a drug that actually does work. Which of the following identifies the error that is generally considered more serious and the value that represents its probability?
A. Type I error; alpha
B. Type I error; beta
C. Type II error; alpha
D. Type II error; beta
E. Type II error; power
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Approving a drug that doesn't work means rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true, which is a Type I error. The Type I error is considered the more serious error, and its probability is alpha.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Hypothesis Testing and Error
Question 1203
A trial compares a new statin with an existing statin for preventing myocardial infarction. The investigators set alpha at 0.05, obtain p = 0.08, fail to reject the null hypothesis, and conclude the drugs are equivalent. A later, larger trial shows the new statin truly is more effective. Which of the following statements best describes the original trial?
A. It made a correct decision because p was greater than alpha
B. It made a Type I error because p was greater than alpha
C. It made a Type II error, and the probability of this error is beta
D. Its alpha was 0.08
E. Its power was 0.92
Answer: C
Why this is correct: There was a real difference (the null hypothesis was false), and the trial failed to reject the null hypothesis. That is a Type II error, and its probability is beta.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1204
A cohort study follows 2,000 factory workers exposed to an industrial solvent and 3,000 unexposed office workers for 10 years. Chronic kidney disease develops in 80 of the exposed workers and 30 of the unexposed workers. Which of the following is the relative risk of chronic kidney disease among exposed workers compared with unexposed workers?
A. 0.03
B. 0.25
C. 1.5
D. 2.7
E. 4.0
Answer: E
Why this is correct: Risk in the exposed = 80/2,000 = 0.04. Risk in the unexposed = 30/3,000 = 0.01. RR = 0.04 / 0.01 = 4.0. Exposed workers have 4 times the risk of kidney disease.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1205
A prospective cohort study follows 2,000 adults aged 65 years for 8 years to evaluate statin use and dementia. The results are as follows: Developed dementia: statin users, 30; nonusers, 90. No dementia: statin users, 970; nonusers, 910. Total: statin users, 1,000; nonusers, 1,000. Which of the following is the relative risk of dementia among statin users compared with nonusers?
A. 0.03
B. 0.31
C. 0.33
D. 1.0
E. 3.0
Answer: C
Why this is correct: The results are grouped by outcome, so pull out each exposure group's numbers before calculating. Risk in statin users = 30/1,000 = 0.03. Risk in nonusers = 90/1,000 = 0.09. RR = 0.03 / 0.09 = 0.33. Statin users had one-third the risk of dementia.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1206
A cohort study of 10,000 adults finds that the relative risk of colon cancer among adults who exercise at least 150 minutes per week, compared with those who exercise less, is 0.6. Which of the following statements best interprets this result?
A. Exercise causes a 60% reduction in colon cancer
B. The odds of exercise among patients with colon cancer are 0.6 times the odds among those without it
C. The risk of colon cancer among those who exercise is 0.6 times the risk among those who don't
D. The risk of colon cancer among those who exercise is 60% higher
E. There is no association between exercise and colon cancer
Answer: C
Why this is correct: The relative risk compares the risk of disease in the exposed group with the risk in the unexposed group. An RR below 1 means the risk of disease is lower in the exposed group.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1207
A case-control study identifies 200 patients with pancreatic cancer and 400 patients without cancer and asks about prior heavy alcohol use. A student divides the proportion of alcohol users who have cancer by the proportion of nonusers who have cancer and reports a relative risk. Which of the following best explains why this calculation is inappropriate?
A. Relative risk can only be calculated when exposure is randomly assigned
B. Relative risk is only used in prospective studies, and this study is retrospective
C. Relative risk requires measuring exposure and disease at a single point in time
D. The odds ratio and relative risk always give identical results
E. The sample size is too small to calculate a relative risk
Answer: B
Why this is correct: In a case-control study, the investigators choose how many people with and without disease to include, so the proportion of each exposure group that has cancer reflects their design, not true risk. Relative risk is only used in prospective studies.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1208
A cohort study enrolls 500 adults who use a certain herbal supplement and 1,500 adults who do not. After 5 years, liver injury has occurred in 50 supplement users and 30 nonusers. Which of the following is the relative risk of liver injury among supplement users compared with nonusers?
A. 0.08
B. 0.2
C. 1.7
D. 5.0
E. 5.4
Answer: D
Why this is correct: Risk in users = 50/500 = 0.10. Risk in nonusers = 30/1,500 = 0.02. RR = 0.10 / 0.02 = 5.0.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1209
In a randomized controlled trial, 2,000 adults with atrial fibrillation are assigned to a new anticoagulant or placebo. After 2 years, stroke occurs in 20 of 1,000 patients in the drug group and 40 of 1,000 patients in the placebo group. Which of the following best describes the relative risk of stroke and its interpretation?
A. 0.02; the drug lowers the risk of stroke by 2 percentage points
B. 0.5; the odds of receiving the drug among patients with stroke are half the odds among those without stroke
C. 0.5; the risk of stroke in the drug group is half the risk in the placebo group
D. 1.0; there is no difference in stroke risk between the groups
E. 2.0; the risk of stroke in the drug group is twice the risk in the placebo group
Answer: C
Why this is correct: Risk in the drug group = 20/1,000 = 0.02. Risk in the placebo group = 40/1,000 = 0.04. RR = 0.02 / 0.04 = 0.5. An RR below 1 means lower risk in the treated (exposed) group.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1210
A cohort study follows 4,000 adults aged 55 years, half of whom drink at least 3 cups of coffee daily, for 12 years. Parkinson disease develops in 80 of the 2,000 coffee drinkers and 80 of the 2,000 non-coffee drinkers. Which of the following best describes the association between coffee intake and Parkinson disease in this study?
A. RR = 0.04; coffee lowers the risk of Parkinson disease
B. RR = 0; coffee completely prevents Parkinson disease
C. RR = 1; coffee causes Parkinson disease in 1% of drinkers
D. RR = 1; the risk of Parkinson disease is equal in both groups
E. RR = 2; coffee doubles the risk of Parkinson disease
Answer: D
Why this is correct: Risk in coffee drinkers = 80/2,000 = 0.04, and risk in non-coffee drinkers = 80/2,000 = 0.04. RR = 0.04 / 0.04 = 1, which means the risk is equal for exposed and unexposed people.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Relative Risk
Question 1211
A research team has received funding to study whether long-term hair dye use is associated with non-Hodgkin lymphoma in women. The team specifically wants to report a relative risk of lymphoma associated with hair dye use. Which of the following study approaches would allow them to calculate a relative risk?
A. Ask 500 women with lymphoma and 1,000 without lymphoma about past hair dye use
B. Follow 20,000 women without lymphoma, grouped by hair dye use, for 15 years
C. Pull charts of 500 women with lymphoma and count how many used hair dye
D. Search pharmacy records of women with and without lymphoma for past hair dye purchases
E. Survey 10,000 women once about current hair dye use and current lymphoma
Answer: B
Why this is correct: Relative risk requires knowing the risk of disease in an exposed group and an unexposed group, which means starting with disease-free people grouped by exposure and following them forward. That's a prospective cohort design.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio
Question 1212
A case-control study enrolls 200 adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and 400 adults without it. Exposure to biomass cooking fuel is reported by 120 of the patients with COPD and 100 of the patients without COPD. Which of the following is the odds ratio for biomass fuel exposure among patients with COPD compared with those without COPD?
A. 0.22
B. 1.2
C. 2.4
D. 2.6
E. 4.5
Answer: E
Why this is correct: Build the 2x2 table first: cases exposed (a) = 120, cases unexposed (c) = 80, controls exposed (b) = 100, controls unexposed (d) = 300. OR = (a × d)/(b × c) = (120 × 300)/(100 × 80) = 36,000/8,000 = 4.5.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio
Question 1213
A case-control study examines household mold exposure and adult-onset asthma. The results are as follows: Asthma: mold exposure, 60; no mold exposure, 40. No asthma: mold exposure, 90; no mold exposure, 210. Which of the following is the odds ratio for mold exposure among patients with asthma compared with those without asthma?
A. 0.29
B. 0.67
C. 1.5
D. 2.5
E. 3.5
Answer: E
Why this is correct: These results are grouped by disease status instead of by exposure, which is flipped from the usual layout, so label the cells before calculating. Odds of exposure among cases = 60/40 = 1.5. Odds of exposure among controls = 90/210 = 0.43. OR = 1.5/0.43 = 3.5, which is the same as (60 × 210)/(40 × 90) = 12,600/3,600.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio

A case-control study of 300 patients with bladder cancer and 600 controls reports an odds ratio of 3.0 for occupational exposure to aromatic amines. Which of the following statements best interprets this result?

D. The odds of aromatic amine exposure are 3 times lower among patients with bladder cancer

Answer: C
Why this is correct: The odds ratio compares the odds of having the exposure among those with the disease to the odds among those without it. An OR above 1 means the exposure is more common among cases.

Why this is correct: An OR below 1 means the odds of having the exposure are lower among those with the disease than among those without it.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio
Question 1216

Why this is correct: The odds ratio can be used in both retrospective and prospective studies. The relative risk is only used in prospective studies.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio
Question 1217

D. 2.0
E. 3.0
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Cases exposed (a) = 100, cases unexposed (c) = 300, controls exposed (b) = 200, controls unexposed (d) = 200. OR = (100 × 200)/(200 × 300) = 20,000/60,000 = 0.33. The odds of sunscreen use are lower among patients with melanoma.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio

C. The odds ratio and relative risk always give the same value

Why this is correct: A case-control study starts with people who do and don't have the disease and looks back for exposure. Because it's retrospective, the odds ratio is the appropriate measure.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Odds Ratio

Answer: E
Why this is correct: Cases exposed (a) = 90, cases unexposed (c) = 60, controls exposed (b) = 60, controls unexposed (d) = 190. OR = (90 × 190)/(60 × 60) = 17,100/3,600 = 4.75.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1220
A new rapid strep antigen test is evaluated in 500 children with sore throat, using throat culture as the gold standard. Of 100 children with a positive culture, 90 have a positive rapid test. Of 400 children with a negative culture, 60 have a positive rapid test. Which of the following is the sensitivity of the rapid test?
A. 0.30
B. 0.60
C. 0.85
D. 0.90
E. 0.97
Answer: D
Why this is correct: Sensitivity is the proportion of people with the disease who are correctly identified: TP/(TP + FN) = 90/(90 + 10) = 0.90.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values

B. 0.60
C. 0.80
D. 0.90
E. 0.96
Answer: B
Why this is correct: PPV is the proportion of people who test positive who actually have the disease: TP/(TP + FP) = 45/(45 + 30) = 0.60.

Answer: D
Why this is correct: These results are grouped by disease status instead of by test result, so match each number to the right cell before calculating. Specificity is the proportion of people without the disease who are correctly identified: TN/(TN + FP) = 255/(255 + 45) = 0.85.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1223
A screening test is applied to 1,000 adults, 100 of whom have the disease. The test is positive in 95 of the 100 people with the disease. It is also positive in 90 of the 900 people without the disease. Which of the following is the negative predictive value of this test?

B. 0.51
C. 0.90
D. 0.95
E. 0.99
Answer: E
Why this is correct: Build the table from the words: TP = 95, FN = 5, FP = 90, TN = 810. NPV is the proportion of people who test negative who don't have the disease: TN/(TN + FN) = 810/(810 + 5) = 0.99.

Question 1226

E. Specificity
Answer: A
Why this is correct: NPV is the proportion of people who test negative who do not have the disease. The starting group in the stem is patients with a negative test.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1227
A surgeon is choosing between two imaging tests to decide which patients should undergo an invasive biopsy for suspected pancreatic cancer. She wants to avoid sending patients who don't have cancer to biopsy. Which of the following properties should be highest for the test she chooses?
A. Negative predictive value
B. Power
C. Prevalence
D. Sensitivity
E. Specificity
Answer: E
Why this is correct: Sending a patient without cancer to biopsy would follow a false-positive result. High specificity means a low chance of false positives, so the test she wants is one with high specificity.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1228
A new screening test for hepatitis C has a sensitivity of 100%. It is used in a large population that includes people with and without hepatitis C. Which of the following results would this test never produce?
A. A negative result in a patient with the disease
B. A negative result in a patient without the disease
C. A positive result in a patient with the disease
D. A positive result in a patient without the disease
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Sensitivity is TP/(TP + FN). A sensitivity of 100% means there are no false negatives, so everyone with the disease tests positive. A negative result in someone with the disease is a false negative.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1229
A new rapid test for a sexually transmitted infection has a sensitivity of 0.90 and a specificity of 0.60 when compared with nucleic acid testing. Which of the following statements about this test is correct?
A. Because sensitivity is high, few patients with the infection will have a false-negative result
B. Because sensitivity is high, few patients without the infection will test positive
C. Because sensitivity is high, most patients who test positive will have the infection
D. Because specificity is low, few patients without the infection will have a false-positive result
E. Because specificity is low, most patients with the infection will be missed
Answer: A
Why this is correct: High sensitivity means a low chance of false negatives, so most infected patients will test positive.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1230
A 47-year-old woman undergoes screening mammography, and the radiologist reads the result as suspicious for malignancy. Core needle biopsy of the area shows benign fibrocystic tissue, and she has no breast cancer on further follow-up. Which of the following best describes her mammography result?
A. False negative
B. False positive
C. True negative
D. True positive
E. Type I error
Answer: B
Why this is correct: A false positive is a person without the disease who tests positive. The mammogram was positive, and she doesn't have cancer.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1231
A new urine test for bladder cancer is evaluated in 500 patients with hematuria, all of whom undergo cystoscopy. The results are as follows: Urine test positive: cancer on cystoscopy, 70; no cancer on cystoscopy, 10. Urine test negative: cancer on cystoscopy, 30; no cancer on cystoscopy, 390. Which of the following measures of this test's validity is lowest?
A. Negative predictive value
B. Positive predictive value
C. Sensitivity
D. Specificity
Answer: C
Why this is correct: Sensitivity = 70/(70 + 30) = 0.70. Specificity = 390/(390 + 10) = 0.975. PPV = 70/(70 + 10) = 0.875. NPV = 390/(390 + 30) = 0.93. Sensitivity is the lowest. Read the lead-in carefully, since it asks for the lowest value.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Sensitivity, Specificity, and Predictive Values
Question 1232
A screening test for a genetic disorder has a sensitivity of 80% and a specificity of 90%. It is applied to 1,000 people: 200 who have the disorder and 800 who do not. Which of the following is the number of false-positive results?
A. 20
B. 40
C. 80
D. 160
E. 720
Answer: C
Why this is correct: False positives come from people without the disorder. Specificity is 90%, so 90% of the 800 test negative (720 true negatives) and 10% test positive: 0.10 × 800 = 80 false positives.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Bias, Correlation, and Confidence Intervals
Question 1233
A single survey of 3,000 adults finds that those who drink more cups of coffee per day report more nights of insomnia per week. A news article based on the survey states that drinking coffee causes insomnia. Which of the following best describes the main problem with the article's conclusion?
A. It commits a Type I error
B. It commits a Type II error
C. It reports the odds ratio instead of the relative risk
D. It treats a correlation as proof of causation
E. It uses a prospective design that cannot measure prevalence
Answer: D
Why this is correct: Correlation reflects the strength and direction of an association between variables. Causation means one event results from the other. A single survey shows the two go together but can't show that coffee causes the insomnia (people who sleep poorly might also drink more coffee).

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Bias, Correlation, and Confidence Intervals
Question 1234
In a study of a new drug for heart failure, physicians at each site are allowed to decide which of their patients receive the new drug and which receive standard therapy. The physicians tend to give the new drug to their younger, healthier patients. The new-drug group has lower mortality. Which of the following best describes the problem with this study?
A. Bias
B. Correlation
C. Low power
D. Type I error
E. Type II error
Answer: A
Why this is correct: Bias introduces a systematic error by selecting or favoring one outcome over others. Healthier patients were put in the new-drug group, which favors a better outcome in that group regardless of the drug. Random assignment, as in an RCT, is how studies remove this bias.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Bias, Correlation, and Confidence Intervals
Question 1235
A randomized trial reports that a new drug lowers LDL cholesterol by an average of 38 mg/dL, with a 95% confidence interval of 33 to 43 mg/dL. Which of the following best describes what the confidence interval indicates?
A. How close the study's result is likely to be to the true effect
B. The power of the study
C. The probability of a Type I error
D. The probability that the null hypothesis is true
E. The proportion of patients whose LDL fell by 33 to 43 mg/dL
Answer: A
Why this is correct: A confidence interval indicates how close research results are to reality, meaning how reliable the estimate is based on statistical theory. A narrow interval like this one suggests a fairly precise estimate.

Foundations of Medicine / Biostatistics / Bias, Correlation, and Confidence Intervals
Question 1236
Investigators studying children's growth report a strong positive correlation between height and shoe size in 2,000 children aged 5 to 12 years. Which of the following best describes what this correlation tells the investigators?
A. That larger shoe size causes greater height
B. The probability that the association is due to chance
C. The proportion of children measured incorrectly
D. The strength and direction of the association between height and shoe size
E. The systematic error introduced by how children were selected
Answer: D
Why this is correct: Correlation reflects the strength and/or direction of the association between two or more variables. A strong positive correlation means taller children tend to have larger shoe sizes.
